page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by the Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The server provisions 64 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 32 physical cores via hyperthreading, paired with 128.0 GB of system memory. This yields a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware features include support for AVX, AVX-512, and AES instructions. The configuration includes no integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent disks, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate a clear split between single-threaded and multi-threaded capabilities. Single-core performance falls within lower percentiles, as observed in stress-ng single-core tests (1103.28) and Geekbench single-core scores (1017.0). In contrast, the high core count delivers solid multi-core capacity, showing average performance in stress-ng multi-core (47219.61) and Geekbench multi-core (10572.0), alongside strong throughput in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 201.55 GB/sec. Memory subsystem bandwidth maintains steady transfer rates, logging 118.53 GB/sec in uncached block reads and 38.35 GB/sec in writes.

Given its resource density and hardware profile, the instance provides cost efficiency for highly parallelized batch jobs rather than latency-sensitive single-threaded operations. Tradeoffs include the complete lack of onboard NVMe storage and modest single-core throughput from the older Xeon architecture. Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.16xlarge is appropriate for multi-threaded compilation, batch data processing, distributed caching nodes, and high-concurrency web serving tiers that operate over network-attached storage.
